Official roadmap (higher authority): The Microsoft Teams integration is under active design and planning with a release target of Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November); a restricted pilot begins October 2026 with select accounts, and only the Slack connector is currently a limited pilot [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. The roadmap explicitly warns that sales playbooks and informal Slack communications may claim the Teams integration is “ready for deployment” or “nearly complete,” and says those claims are a contradiction [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. The sales playbook also instructs reps not to guarantee launch dates and states the roadmap places Teams in planning/design for Q4 2026 [NL-009#NL-009-S08]. Engineering planning confirms Teams stays in design for Q4 with development in early 2027, not an immediate release [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

Informal sales/Slack claims: Marcus Reed told a prospect the Teams integration is “basically right around the corner,” has a working connector “almost ready for general release,” and could be included in a July pilot [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. In Slack, he asked for a pilot by July/August, told another prospect it was “basically right around the corner,” and called it a “simple chat wrapper” [NL-027#NL-027-S02]. He also proposed packaging the existing demo as an “alpha” or building a hardcoded custom container for Meridian [NL-027#NL-027-S04].

The Slack thread shows the informal claims are false: the existing demo is only a basic webhook with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and zero citation formatting; engineers call it a “toy” and a security nightmare [NL-027#NL-027-S03]. Product and infrastructure teams rejected the alpha/custom build because of multi-tenant security, compliance, and CI/CD risks [NL-027#NL-027-S04]. Customer Success noted that telling prospects Teams is “almost ready” creates a major expectation gap [NL-027#NL-027-S04].

In summary, the official roadmap treats Teams integration as a planned future release for Q4 2026, while informal sales and Slack claims overstate it as nearly complete and available for immediate pilots; the evidence shows the connector is only an early proof-of-concept not ready for deployment.
